question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x(t))+\operatorname{ln}⁡(y(t)^{2}+1) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5y(t)+{tan}^{-1}⁡(x(t))\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the behavior of the system's solutions near the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\text{ }0]^{T}?$

$\,$
The equilibrium is an 
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1) \\ 5y+{tan}^{-1}⁡(x)\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1))=2+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\ \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}+1))=\frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5y+{tan}^{-1}⁡(x))=\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5y+{tan}^{-1}⁡(x))=5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2+\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & \frac{2y}{{y}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}} & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
\text{\boldsymbol}{f}^{′}({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0) & \frac{2(0)}{(0)^{2}+1} \\ \frac{1}{1+(0)^{2}} & 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), so the system is almost linear at ${x}^{∗}.$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(5-\lambda ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=3,\text{ }5.$

Finally, since we both have two real and positive eigenvalues,, our equilibrium is an $\text{unstable}$ $\text{source}.$
